struct.name: IB_DATA
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The interface buffer holds 64 queued writes. The specification's table names 128 entries, but its address half sits 512 bytes above the data half, which leaves room for 64 doublewords of data, and shipped software walks a ring of 64 (RE_IB_ENTRIES). Each queued write has a data doubleword and an address doubleword; the address half is decoded below. The window shares its low offsets with the CRIME CPU-interface registers, so the rendering engine registers live in their own address space.

struct.name: IB_ADDR
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings

struct.name: IB_CTL
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The specification names this word's thresholds in its interface-buffer section. Above the stall level, host writes stall for the stall count, given in 66 MHz cycles. Above the interrupt level, the host receives an interrupt; it then either polls the status register until the level falls or enables the buffer-empty interrupt (established, [spec] PDF 185). The specification gives no bit layout for these thresholds, so the field bits below stay inferred.

struct.name: IB_RESET
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings

struct.name: TLB_FB_A
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The frame-buffer tables A, B and C each hold 64 doublewords, the texture table 28 and the clip-ID table 4. Shipped software loads all of them with 64-bit stores. A frame-buffer, texture or clip-ID doubleword holds four 16-bit tile entries, tile column 0 in bits 63:48. The entry is the physical address of a 64 KiB tile shifted right by 16 (the page number counted in 64 KiB units). Shipped software sets the top bit of each frame-buffer and texture entry it uses and writes clip-ID entries without it, so the top bit is inferred to be a valid bit (and doubles as address bit 31 of the tile). The register index of tile (x, y) in a frame-buffer table is y * 4 + x / 4. The linear tables further down use 32-bit entries.

struct.name: BUFMODE_SRC
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The pixel pipeline group starts at the base of its own 4 KiB window. Sizes and the read/write column are the specification's register table. The specification lists the vertex and stepper registers as 32 or 64 bits and shipped software writes adjacent 32-bit registers with one 64-bit store (the GL vertex pair, for one). The transfer source stride is absent from the specification's table; the public NetBSD driver and shipped software both write it, so it is established from them. Registers marked w are written only; the others read back. Global registers apply once the pipe has drained, non-global ones per primitive ([spec] PDF 164). Writing any pixel pipeline register with the start-alias bit set commits the queued state as one primitive. Writes after that commit do not change the committed primitive, and committed primitives run in commit order, each to completion (established, [spec] PDF 186, printed 7-30).

struct.name: BUFMODE_DST
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings

struct.name: CLIPMODE
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The specification's table (established, [spec] PDF 173, Table 7-6) puts the enable for screen mask 0 at bit 9 and for mask 4 at bit 5, with the inside-select (scrMaskMode) for mask 0 at bit 4 and for mask 4 at bit 0. The kernel sets bit 5 plus i and bit i for rectangle i (docs/context.md), which is the reverse order. Which order the engine uses is unknown. The fields below give the bit ranges only.

struct.name: DRAWMODE
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc:
Point and rectangle primitives are always flat shaded, whatever the shade bit (16) says. Their colour is the foreground colour register alone (established, [spec] PDF 200, section 7.3.7.1). Triangles and lines are smooth shaded only when bit 16 is set.
The specification's table gives bit 8 as logic-op enable and bit 9 as dither (established, [spec] PDF 174, Table 7-7). The fields below follow the drivers, which use the reverse. That conflict is not settled; see docs/pixel-arithmetic.md.

struct.name: SCRMASK
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Screen mask n is one rectangle in framebuffer coordinates, not window coordinates (established, [spec] PDF 176, Table 7-11). Its fields are the same as the scissor's. The enable and inside-select bits are in ClipMode; see the note there for the order in which the bits pair with the masks.

struct.name: SCISSOR
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Scissor rectangle in window coordinates. The minimum edges are inclusive and the maximum edges exclusive. DrawMode bit 20 enables the test (established, [spec] PDF 176, Table 7-10).

struct.name: WINOFFSET_SRC
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Window-to-framebuffer offset for the read window (established, [spec] PDF 175 to 176, Table 7-9, the WinOffset format). The specification does not say whether the two halves are signed. The kernel writes each half as the window origin minus 4096 (see docs/context.md), so the sign convention is unknown.

struct.name: WINOFFSET_DST
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Window-to-framebuffer offset for the drawing window (established, [spec] PDF 175 to 176, Table 7-9). The layout and the sign question are the same as for the source offset (the read window's register).

struct.name: PRIMITIVE
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc:
The specification gives line_width as the subpixel line width divided by two (established, [spec] PDF 175, Table 7-8). Bits 23:19 are reserved in the specification. DrawMode bit 19, which enables line stipple, is a separate control and does not appear in the primitive word.
The unit of the line width is unknown. The specification's six-bit subpixel precision (established, [spec] PDF 159) is listed for OpenGL rasterization, not for X lines. The public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver's register header calls the field half pixels (inferred, software expectation). Which scale the X engine uses is unknown. See docs/de-2d-drawing.md.

struct.name: VERTEX_X
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: In X mode the host gives each coordinate as a 16-bit unsigned value, in the range [0, 2^16) (established, [spec] PDF 197). The specification does not say how the two coordinates share a vertex word. The public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver puts X in bits 31:16 and Y in bits 15:0 (inferred, software expectation). See docs/de-2d-drawing.md.

struct.name: VERTEX_GL
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc:
Table 7-3 lists each GL vertex word as 32 bits, non-global and write-only, in 13.6 fixed point (established, [spec] PDF 166). The GL-mode text on PDF 197 instead gives 13.4 unsigned fixed point over [0, 2^13) (established). The feature list on PDF 159 gives 6-bit subpixel precision, which fits the 13.6 reading. The two engine descriptions conflict. Which one the engine implements is unknown.
Start-alias stores (inferred, software expectation, docs/inventory/mmio.tsv). The scan records 32-bit stores through the start alias of the x and y words of Vertex.GL[0] and Vertex.GL[1]. It records 64-bit alias stores to Vertex.GL[0].x and Vertex.GL[1].x as well, and no alias store to any Vertex.GL[2] word. The 64-bit alias stores are not explained, so the alias width is unsettled.
Readback extents (inferred, software expectation). A GL readback of a rectangle writes inclusive pixel indices, not the half-open edges of the scissor: the far x is the start x plus the programmed copy width minus one, and the far y is the start y minus the row count plus one, each as (index << 6) & 0x7ffff. A one-row readback therefore writes equal y words and still copies one row. Only driver writes show this. How the engine resolves a fractional edge is unknown. See docs/pixel-transfer.md.

struct.name: XFER_SRC_ADDR
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Readback source start (inferred, software expectation). For a readback from a buffer H rows high, the driver writes the x component as the window x and the y component as H - 1 - window y, each masked to 11 bits. The 0x21000 window bias drops out under that mask. For a 128-row buffer, y = 127 - window y. The equation that combines this packed start with SrcWinOffset is unknown. See docs/pixel-transfer.md.

struct.name: XFER_DST_STRIDE
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Readback row-end increment (inferred, software expectation). With S bytes per pixel, a scratch row pitch P and a programmed copy width C, the driver writes S + max(P - C * S, 0). The row pitch is then (C - 1) * S + that value, which equals P. The width C is the aligned width, not the requested width: the driver rounds it up until the row is a multiple of eight bytes, so a requested width of 15 at four bytes per pixel programs 16. See docs/pixel-transfer.md.

struct.name: STIPPLE_MODE
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Stipple sequence state: the starting pattern index, the maximum pattern index, the starting repeat count and the maximum repeat count (established, [spec] PDF 177, Table 7-12). The specification's reserved range is 23:20, which includes bit 20, the top bit of max_index. max_index is therefore inferred (conflict). The specification does not say what the sequence does after max_index, so that behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: STIPPLE_PATTERN
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The specification gives the pattern as one 32-bit word (established, [spec] PDF 166, Table 7-3). It does not say which bit is drawn first or where a glyph row sits in the word. The public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver places an 8-bit font row at bits 31:24 and a 16-bit row at bits 31:16 (inferred, software expectation), so rows fill the high end of the word. Sample order within the word is unknown. See docs/de-2d-drawing.md.

struct.name: FG_COLOR
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Flat-shaded colour for triangles and lines with DrawMode shade bit 16 clear, and for points and rectangles always. The engine assigns this one value to every fragment (established, [spec] PDF 200, section 7.3.7.1). Colour index flat shading loads an 8-bit index for 8-bit pixels and a 12-bit index for 16-bit and 32-bit pixels. RGBA flat shading loads an RGBA8 value whatever the pixel depth (established, [spec] PDF 200).

struct.name: TEX_MODE
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, PDF 178-179, Table 7-13
struct.doc: Texture mode register, 32 bits (established, [spec] PDF 178-179, Table 7-13). Bits 31:25 are reserved. The fields below carry the table's bit ranges and names. Enumerated values are the table's own; encodings it marks reserved have no name here.

struct.name: TEX_FORMAT
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, PDF 179, Table 7-14
struct.doc: Texture format word, 64 bits (established, [spec] PDF 179, Table 7-14). Bits 63:48 are reserved. The table names six fields and their bit ranges but gives no description for any of them, so what each field computes is unknown here.

struct.name: TEX_STFLAGS
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: tex_stflags sits between tex_qs and tex_dsqdx and is absent from the specification's register table, which skips from the one to the other. Shipped software computes one flag per texture coordinate for each textured triangle from range tests on the vertex values, writes the s flag in bit 0 and the t flag in bit 1 with a 32-bit store, and scales the start and slope values of a flagged coordinate by 2^39 instead of 2^43. Inferred: a set flag tells the engine that coordinate's stepper carries four fewer fraction bits. The layout is established; that meaning is inferred.

struct.name: AA_LINE
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Antialiasing applies only to point and line primitives and only to RGB(A) pixels. It acts on alpha after fogging and before the alpha test. For antialiased lines the specification assumes a line width of two (established, [spec] PDF 206, section 7.3.7.10). The coverage value is a 0.8 fixed-point number, computed from a 128 by 8 slope-and-distance table and a 128 by 4-bit endpoint table, both in ROM (established, [spec] PDF 206-207). The ROM contents are not published, so they are unknown. The register map gives this word as a 2.12 two's complement value for both the slope and the ideal minor coordinate (established, [spec] register map, PDF 169). The antialiasing register table on PDF 180 gives the same bit split but calls both halves 2.14 (established), and the prose on PDF 207 says 2.12. docs/opengl.md reads both halves as 2.14, the precision the driver's arithmetic uses. The precision is not resolved here. The bit split below is the one PDF 180 and the driver reads share. The driver reduces the ideal minor coordinate modulo four pixels (inferred, docs/opengl.md).

struct.name: AA_COV
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The register map gives this word as the start and end endpoint coverage values, each a 7-bit value (established, [spec] register map, PDF 169). The published text does not place them within the word. The split below is a software reading (inferred, docs/opengl.md): the driver writes values from 1 to 64, which fit in 7 bits, with the start value in bits 15:8 and the end value in bits 7:0.

struct.name: ALPHATEST
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Alpha test function and reference. Bits 31:12 are reserved in the specification. The test runs on fragment alpha after antialias coverage and only for RGB(A) pixels, and it is enabled by DrawMode bit 11. A fragment whose comparison fails is discarded.

struct.name: BLEND_COLOR
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Blend constant colour, read and written as a 32-bit word (established, [spec] register map, PDF 169, which names it "blend RGBA constant color"). The constant-color and constant-alpha factor codes of Blend.func select it. The specification does not draw its per-byte layout, so the byte order is unknown.

struct.name: BLEND_FUNC
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Blend equation and factors. The source factor table has a SRC_ALPHA_SATURATE row with no factor given, and the destination factor table has no such code (established absence, [spec] Tables 7-20 and 7-21, PDF 208-209). The specification's factor arithmetic therefore omits it. It also gives no clamp for ADD or SUBTRACT. Both are unknown here; see docs/pixel-arithmetic.md.

struct.name: LOGICOP
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The register's own field table is empty in the specification (section 7.3.1.17). The sixteen bitwise operations are listed in Table 7-23 (established, [spec] PDF 210-211, section 7.3.7.14), and docs/pixel-arithmetic.md gives them. The operation acts on the source colour after dithering and the destination read from the frame buffer. The numeric code for each operation comes from the drivers, not the specification.

struct.name: COLORMASK
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings

struct.name: DEPTH_FUNC
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Depth comparison and clear-depth word. The specification omits the field encoding (established, [spec] PDF 169-170). The field layout below is inferred from the words the shipped driver stores here. Bits 31:28 have no established meaning.

struct.name: DEPTH_ZS
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Start depth of a triangle or depth span, a 25.12 two's complement value with the fraction in the low 12 bits (established, [spec] PDF 169-170 and 212-213). Written through its start alias, which commits the queued primitive. The depth derivatives below use the same format.

struct.name: DEPTH_DZDX
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Depth step in x, 25.12 two's complement (established, [spec] PDF 169-170). Written through its start alias, as for the start depth.

struct.name: DEPTH_DZDY
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Depth step in y, 25.12 two's complement (established, [spec] PDF 169-170). Written through its start alias, as for the start depth.

struct.name: STENCIL_MODE
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Stencil test and update word. The specification leaves its field table empty (established, [spec] PDF 182). The field positions below are inferred from the words the shipped driver stores here. The six operation names are established from [spec] Table 7-27 (PDF 214), but the specification's stencil section is marked TBD. Its orientation of the comparison conflicts with the API and the driver; see docs/pixel-arithmetic.md. Written through its start alias.

struct.name: STENCIL_MASK
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Stencil write mask. The driver writes either 0 or 0xff here on its depth path (inferred). Only bits 7:0 are the mask; bits 31:8 have no established meaning. Written through its start alias, as for the start depth.

struct.name: PIXPIPE_FLUSH

struct.name: STATUS
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The status register is read with 32-bit loads. Shipped software polls the combined idle bit (28), reads the interface-buffer fill level from bits 24:18 to count free slots (64 minus the level) and reads the start and write pointers when saving queued writes on a context switch. The read pointer (17:12) and the setup and pixel-pipe idle bits (27, 26) are taken from the public NetBSD driver and no shipped software reads them. Bit 25 is the memory transfer engine idle bit in the NetBSD driver; the OpenBSD driver names the same bit ready and never reads it. The kernel's transfer-wait routine tests bit 25, which fits an idle reading, so the position is established and the meaning inferred. The start field (5:0) is where the entries not yet committed begin; its meaning is inferred. The specification's register map lists the status registers as a user-space region, placed after the MTE registers in the rendering block (established, [spec] PDF 162).

struct.name: IB_DISCARD
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: ib_discard sits two doublewords above the status register. Shipped kernel code stores zero to it with a 32-bit store, never reads it, and does so after saving the outgoing client's queued writes on a context switch, after the incoming client's loads, and at the end of each translation table loader. The user-mode library and the X server never write it. Inferred: the write discards the queued writes not yet committed. The register's position and its write-zero use are established; that effect is inferred.

struct.name: BUFMODE
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The buffer mode words (source and destination share one layout) pick the buffer, its TLB and the pixel format. buf_type chooses tiled access through a frame-buffer table or linear access through a linear table; buf_depth is the word size in memory and pix_depth the pixel size, which must not exceed it. ycrcb is valid in the source word only. Shipped software writes the values in the vectors below; other bits are reserved (one shipped swap path sets bit 30 as well). The specification's register tables (established, [spec] PDF 171-172) mark bits 31:13 reserved and give them no function. They also mark buf_type 3 and 6 and pix_type 4 to 14 reserved, and list only depth values 0 to 2 for buf_depth and pix_depth, so value 3 of either depth field is not defined. Whether the hardware ignores bits 31:13 on write or returns them on read is unknown; no shipped software or published source depends on it. When doublePix is set, doublePixSel says which half of the word is selected (established, [spec] PDF 171-172). The specification does not say which bit value picks the front half and which the back, so that mapping is unknown. The pixel figure (established, [spec] PDF 188, figure 7-5 in section 7.3.4.3) draws no 32-bit RGB layout. It shows CI8, CI12, RG3_B2, A1_RGB5 and RGBA8 only. So the bit positions of red, green and blue for pix_type 1 at 32 bits are unknown, and so is whether the low byte is unused. Routes tried: that figure. Not yet tried: the 32-bit RGB paths in the public NetBSD driver and in shipped libGLcore readbacks.

struct.name: IBADDR_HI
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: ib_addr holds the address half of each queued write. Software decodes its upper 32 bits (IBADDR_HI, the word at the register's own address in big-endian layout) as the register's doubleword index within its group, the group, a byte lane code and one flag bit; the hardware meaning of the lane code and the flag is inferred. The index is address bits 10:3 and the group is address bits 14:12 of the register; bit 11, the start alias, is the address bit left out, so the flag is inferred to mark an entry written through the start alias. Replay by software writes lane 3 as one doubleword, lane 2 as the first (upper) data word at the register address, lane 1 as the second data word four bytes higher, and treats lane 0 as an error that writes nothing. The lower 32 bits are not decoded by any shipped software read.

struct.name: LINENT
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Each doubleword holds two 32-bit page entries, the even page in the upper word and the odd page in the lower word. Software indexes a table with address bits 16:13 and stores a page number with its top bit set, which is inferred to be a valid bit. LINENT describes one such entry.

struct.name: PIXEL_A1_RGB5
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: 16-bit RGB(A) colour pixel, named A1_RGB5 in the specification: alpha in bit 15, red in bits 14:10, green in bits 9:5 and blue in bits 4:0 (established, [spec] PDF 188, figure 5 in section 7.3.4.3). The NetBSD crmfb driver describes 16-bit raster operations as 5:5:5 with red at bit 11, green at 6 and blue at 1 (software expectation, public driver). That places the fields differently. The conflict is not resolved here. Its pixel type and depth codes are rgba and bits16 in BUFMODE (inferred, on the same basis as RG3_B2).

struct.name: PIXEL_RG3_B2
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: 8-bit RGB colour pixel, named RG3_B2 (332) in the specification: red in bits 7:5, green in bits 4:2 and blue in bits 1:0, with no alpha field (established, [spec] PDF 188, figure 7-5 in section 7.3.4.3). Its pixel type and depth codes are rgb and bits8 in BUFMODE (inferred: the figure gives the name and depth but does not print the codes).

struct.name: PIXEL_RGBA8
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: 32-bit RGBA colour pixel, named RGBA8 in the specification (8888): red in bits 31:24, green in bits 23:16, blue in bits 15:8 and alpha in bits 7:0 (established, [spec] PDF 188, figure 5 in section 7.3.4.3). Its pixel type and depth codes are rgba and bits32 in BUFMODE (inferred, on the same basis as RG3_B2).

struct.name: SCRMASK_HI
struct.from: published CRIME 1.5 draft specification, public NetBSD O2 framebuffer driver, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Each screen mask is one clip rectangle; the end coordinates are exclusive. The upper word (SCRMASK_HI, at the register's own address in big-endian layout) holds the start corner and the lower word (SCRMASK_LO) the end corner.
